The Washington knowledge test

  • 40 multiple-choice questions.
  • You need 32 correct answers to pass (80%).
  • The state also gives the test in Spanish.

5 sample questions

1. In Washington, how many questions are on the knowledge test?

  1. 25 questions
  2. 40 questions (correct answer)
  3. 50 questions
  4. 20 questions

Answer: B. The Washington knowledge test has 40 questions.

2. In Washington, may a driver with an instruction permit or intermediate license use a phone hands-free?

  1. Yes, any time
  2. No, only in an emergency (correct answer)
  3. Yes, at red lights
  4. Yes, for short calls

Answer: B. In Washington permit and intermediate license holders may not use a wireless device at all, even hands-free, except in an emergency.

Washington handbook, page §1.8.

3. In Washington, if you cannot move over a lane for a stopped emergency vehicle, how much must you slow down?

  1. 5 mph below the limit
  2. To 15 mph
  3. Not at all
  4. At least 10 mph below the posted limit (correct answer)

Answer: D. In Washington, if you cannot safely move over one lane, you must slow to at least 10 mph below the posted speed limit.

Washington handbook, page §4.17.

4. In Washington, after a full stop at a red light, when may you turn left on red if no sign forbids it?

  1. Never
  2. Only from a one-way street onto a two-way street
  3. From a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street going left (correct answer)
  4. From any street onto any street

Answer: C. In Washington, after stopping and yielding, you may turn left on red from a one-way or two-way street onto a one-way street that carries traffic to the left, unless a sign forbids it.

Washington handbook, page §4.11.

5. In Washington, a person is walking across the street in front of you. They are not using a cane, wheelchair, or service animal. When may you drive on?

  1. As soon as they pass your front bumper
  2. When they reach the middle of the street
  3. When they have cleared your lane and one more lane (correct answer)
  4. When they step off the curb

Answer: C. In Washington, you must wait until a person crossing has cleared your lane and one more lane before you drive on.

Washington handbook, page §4.1.
